title: Japan Goodies: ordering from Japan without the confusion
situation: A personal-shopping service for items from Japan. Customers needed to request items, track orders, and know when things would actually arrive, not just that they had ordered.
built: Type-in quantities, per-order arrival dates (ETA), stock that deducts and restores correctly, notifications for every status change, and an admin report generator.
result: No more overselling stock that is not there, and customers see an arrival-sorted list instead of asking for updates. All five requested updates shipped and passed 27 of 27 end-to-end checks on a test database.
tech: PHP 8 + MySQL on XAMPP with HTML/CSS/JS. Orders store estimated_arrival; inventory is real stock via products.quantity with stock_deducted flags so cancellations restore exactly once and oversell returns HTTP 409. A notifications table + api/notifications.php drives the header badge and updates page. Reports follow the sequence Report, arrival day, item, pre-order, exportable to CSV and print. Also produced a 132-case peer-evaluation paper matched against the actual system behaviour.

title: Damath: the maths board game, rebuilt so a game can actually finish
situation: Damath blends checkers-style captures with arithmetic. The existing game crashed on its hardest AI levels and its puzzle mode was broken, which is frustrating for anyone trying to practise.
built: Fixed the Hard and Expert AI crashes and the puzzle mode, corrected multi-capture move generation, and added undo, a winner screen with Rematch and Menu, a rules summary before each game, and capture-rule options.
result: It now plays from start to finish at every difficulty, works fully offline (on purpose, as requested), and lets a single player choose Red, Blue, or random on Expert.
tech: Python + Pygame, a single codebase of roughly 4,900 lines. Settings rebuilt as a card layout to fix UI overlaps; side selection and rule variants (optional / max-capture / dama-first) are configurable per match. Shipped with assets and automated tests covering move generation and the previously crashing AI paths (v5.1 polish, v5.2 rules and settings round).

title: My portfolio and game arcade: from static pages to a small system
situation: My first portfolio was static. Adding a project meant editing HTML by hand, game scores vanished on refresh, and one bug made the Space key stop working in the typing game.
built: Added a PHP backend with an admin login for adding projects, top-10 leaderboards for every game, pun descriptions, three new games, a live Manila clock, and smoother page motion. Found and fixed the Space bug: Snake’s page-wide key handler was swallowing it.
result: Projects are managed from a form instead of code, scores persist, and the site is versioned on GitHub. This site is its successor: same content, explained for everyone.
tech: Vanilla PHP + SQLite (api/, no MySQL setup needed), first-run admin creation with no default password, projects seeded from the original 17 cards. Leaderboards fall back to localStorage when PHP is not running so the static mirror never breaks. Code lives at github.com/otep808/portfolio (branch yep).
